verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both averages are defined, with the paper's constants: the angular one divides ∫_0^{2π} by 2π and holds the remaining arguments (including the auxiliary point) fixed, since in use the base point of `angularAverage` is a lifted chart point `(x.1, (x.2.1, Y))` that already carries Y; the auxiliary one is the iterated unit-square integral holding all slow arguments fixed. Rewriting: the Lean models T² = ℝ²/ℤ² by unit-periodic functions on the plane integrated over [0,1]², so the paper's normalization ∫_{T²} 1 dY' = 1 is the content of `torusMean_const` at c = 1, and `torusMean_eq_haar` identifies the unit-square integral with the integral against the normalized Haar measure `torusMeasure` on the quotient torus. The cleanest match for the second line of (3.7) is `UniformFourierAlias.parameterMean f p = torusMean (fun Y => f (p, Y))`, which holds an arbitrary slow parameter p fixed by its signature and averages over Y alone. One field type also carries all of the paper's arguments concretely and both averages act on it: with `Lift S = ℝ × (S × Plane)` (PressureStream.lean:26), `liftedTorusAverage` averages a field on `Lift P` over the Y slot of its own point with every slow coordinate fixed — the paper's second line of (3.7), in the paper's argument layout — while `angularAverage` is applied at `D = LocalSignedRequest.Point = PressureStream.Lift Plane` (LocalSignedRequest.lean:24) in `SignedMeanGain.meanBar_symmetricCovariance`, i.e. to a field of (slow, Y, θ) with Y held fixed. The only residual difference is of packaging: the two operators are declared in different namespaces and at different generality (angular average over any chart D plus an angle, torus average over ℝ × S plus the plane), so neither declaration mentions the other and they are composed at the point of use.
